speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; this is a serious situation. To determine the cause, I need to ask you: Are there any known risk factors such as maternal fever, chorioamnionitis, or lack of prenatal care? Also, has the baby had any difficulty breathing or poor feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) secondary to perinatal asphyxia. Given the history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and immediate-onset seizures, I am also concerned for sepsis; I will request a blood culture and CBC to rule this out before finalizing the plan.
